title: lunarsim-scene v1 (scene.json, the package index)
description: A 3D replay of one simulated year (writer lunarsim/scene.py; Python reader scene.read / scene.position). The package folder holds scene.json, routes.bin and chunk_NNN.bin. Binaries are little-endian float32 matrices. routes.bin: per item in routes.items, n rows x route_columns (x, y, z, f) at byte `offset`; f is the cumulative time fraction along the route. chunk_NNN.bin: segments (rows x segment_columns) at segments.offset, then hourly series (rows x hourly_columns) at hourly.offset, the first row being hour hourly.first_hour. A vehicle's segments cover [0, horizon_h] without gaps; a segment with route >= 0 moves along routes.items[route] from f0 to f1, f linear in time; route = -1 moves on the straight line (x0, y0, z0) -> (x1, y1, z1) (stationary when both are equal). state indexes `states`; job indexes `jobs` (-1 = idle or parked). Segments are split at chunk boundaries and at Earth-link waits.

hourly_columns.description: sun_az_deg, night (0/1), earth_el_deg, earth_radius_deg, earth_bearing_deg (BASE, ground level; NaN without the Earth track), then waiting_n_<site> and waiting_kg_<site> for every site in `sites` order (items ready and not yet picked up at the start of the hour)

trajectory.description: the B-33 episode (data/policies/trajectories-v1.json) of the classical law for this class whose |miss| is nearest; a failed landing points to the first-failure episode

deliveries.description: [t_h, site index into `sites`, mass_kg as the trace's cargo table gives it]
